useRenderable compares combined entity generations through Renderer. Mutating component data without a generation change will not notify a subscriber.

snapshot.ts copies every entity of a world into plain data and restores a world from it. Saved games use it, see saving.

Exported sprites are stored as { $sprite: "exportName" }. Game code compares sprites by identity, such as entity[SPRITE] === none, so loading returns the same exported object. Generated sprites, such as recolored ones, are stored as data.

The result must be stored with structured cloning, as IndexedDB does, to keep shared objects and values like Infinity. JSON would lose both.

restoreSnapshot creates a world and recreates the entities in their original order with restoreEntity, so IDs and query order stay the same. Afterwards, install systems with createSystems and call preloadLevel, as for a generated level. Systems start with fresh internal state and lazily initialize cells around the hero again.

generate(width, height, forced) retries contradictions up to five times and returns undefined if none succeeds. Forced entries are [x, y, tileName]. Adjacency stops at the layout edges rather than wrapping.
Normal text is handled by the chat dialog. Controls and the chat popup gate command input behind TEST_MODE. The documentation imports the registry rather than maintaining a separate set of names.

Description callbacks are evaluated lazily to avoid circular initialization between sprite and balancing modules. Derived descriptions use current equipment/consumption rules, rather than a separate text copy of their values.

Start them with npcSequence from sequence helpers. The shared step helper runs entry work once and advances when the step condition completes. Store progress in state.args.memory so it remains part of saved snapshots.

pixelFrame in pixels.ts builds character frames. Keyboard key and socket sprites are defined in sprites/particles.ts and composed by components/Keyboard.
step changes lastStep only after entry succeeds. Completing a step selects onLeave(); END_STEP finishes the sequence.
buildConstructions is the plan registry used by the hammer dialog and Build. Each entry describes one construction and all its variants.

Do not mutate classDefinitions to change one hero. Call getClassData, then populate that entity from the result. Leveling supplies level growth; the initial class definition is not a level-10 stat table.

With no resource key, getHarvestConfig returns zero work and no yields. Configured resources begin with amount === maximum. Tool stats determine how much work an action can apply; Farmable records later crop stages.

generateUnitData fills missing unit stats, sets maximum HP/MP from the initial stats and resolves harvesting work. Its drop selection uses randomness; callers needing repeatable output must seed randomness through the test harness.
Matrices are column-first: matrix[x][y]. Level matrices are square and their access helpers wrap coordinates at the edges.

createMatrix reuses its value rather than cloning it. Use matrixFactory for independent objects in each cell. Use square matrices with mapMatrix; its current output allocation swaps the input dimensions.
Map keeps duplicated walkability entries in sync with setPath.
Game randomness uses Math.random. Tests replace it with a seeded generator through the test environment.

index.ts creates and upgrades saved games and keeps a list of save summaries for the menu. storage.ts stores them in the browser's IndexedDB. Players find the controls in Savegames.

A save is a summary plus a world snapshot. The summary holds the package version, level, class, hair color, hero level, equipped items, playtime, kills and deaths for the saves dialog. Its name is the local time in YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS format, 15 characters that fill a popup row next to the hero sprite.
Playtime counts world updates outside the main menu. Kills and deaths are totals of the whole game in the player component, unlike defeatedUnits, which is reset per level for quests.

The summaries are kept in memory, latest first, because popups render synchronously. They are read once on start and updated after each save or erase. Erasing removes the summary right away and deletes the stored save through world.metadata.eraseGame.

The Continue portal of the main menu has a load popup tab. setContinuePortal only adds its vortex and popup while saves are listed. The menu sequence updates it when summaries finish loading after the menu was generated, or when the last save is erased. Confirming a save runs initiateLoad, which plays the first half of a warp: the hero steps into the portal and vision closes. After the loading screen appears, the World component restores the world, installs systems and switches to it. The restored world continues exactly as it was saved, without the vision opening of a new world. Children of the World component remount for the new world, and the camera starts at the restored viewpoint.

storage.ts stores saved worlds in the browser's IndexedDB database alive. The summaries store holds menu entries; saves holds complete snapshots. Both use the save ID as their key and are updated in one transaction.
storeGame requests persistent browser storage. The browser may decline; clearing site data still removes saves. See saved games and snapshots.
Documentation browser tests check the imported examples, pause/reset controls, navigation, page errors, and small-screen layout. See documentation tools.
Refreshes after a reference generation changes and writes target IDs into Actionable. Blocking entities are checked before targets behind them in the same cell.
Patterns keep their own memory and may add or remove patterns. Movement and Trigger consume the resulting intent later in the update. NPC story stages are defined in NPC sequences.
Shootable belongs to targets, not shooters. Its arrow count is recovered by Drop. Projectile travel state is shared with the running Sequence.

Checks lastInteraction so the same generation cannot also move or attack. Buildable stores the finished cell; Stats stores progress. Plans, costs and ground restrictions come from building data.

It skips an already consumed generation and units that cannot interact. Clickable marks the pending target; Bumpable distinguishes repeated attempts. The resulting action is consumed by Interact, or its direction reaches Movement.

A collector needs Collectable, inventory, stats and movement. Work runs on its action generation, and is skipped while another collection or interaction is already using that action.

When installing systems on a restored world, initialize cached vision, haste and equipment stats from the saved hero. Loading must not add bonuses again. See saved games and the received-state effects in Magic.

calculateDamage preserves fractional health. Positive offense minus defense is dealt directly; otherwise damage is 1 / (2 - delta). A nonpositive attack deals zero. The returned hp is the precise value; damage is the displayed change.
Push and Spike run before melee; Movement runs after it. Shared helpers are also used by Magic and Ballistics.
Runs after Movement, and checks the relevant entity generation before repeating work. Visibility then applies the resulting inside/outside view.
Soul holds revival data; Spawnable holds the return point and appearance. This runs before Drop, so the tombstone and respawn state exist before inventory cleanup.
isControllable is shared with action systems so frozen units cannot act. Snow uses Coverable; immersion and appearance changes are completed by Immersion.

Runs first in the system order. Level keeps cell data separate from its initialized flags; Map registers the resulting entities. initializeCell is also available to code that needs a particular cell immediately.
Action discovers targets before this system runs. Stale interactions are cleared when their target disappears or becomes invalid. Dialog selection itself is handled by Popup.
The cast's target history prevents unintended repeated hits. Damage supplies shared combat helpers; Burn, Freeze and Sequence advance the effects.

Displaced units and mobs are processed before the player. Push, Spike and Damage run before normal movement and can consume the action. Terrain tempo and equipment haste affect the reference interval. Position changes use Map.

Create dialogs with createPopup: it initializes selection arrays and a priority-90 camera viewpoint. closePopup and removePopup handle the matching cleanup. Popup data describes the state shape.
Pushable belongs to the actor; Displacable belongs to the moved object. Push runs before Damage and Movement.

The actor is checked once per action generation and cannot have interacted already. getSpikable reads the target's current combined spike stat; legacy Spikable data does not supply it. Damage uses the shared combat calculation, and an active bubble can absorb the hit.
Runs before melee and Movement, so contact can consume the attempted move.
Popup receives dialog input next. Fishing, Build, Harvest and Magic advance the resulting actions.

Runs before normal Movement, which skips movement already consumed by the vessel action.

The elapsed clock advances every update. On restore it starts at the latest existing liquid timestamp, so saved bubbles can finish instead of waiting on a clock reset. See saved games. Water terrain uses Immersible; its animated effects use Liquid.

getBlockable in Action checks this marker before choosing another target in the cell. Solid movement obstacles use Collidable.
Build replaces the plot with cell once its Stats reach hp === maxHp. Progress is stored in Stats, not Buildable.
Click, Movement and combat use the bump generation and direction to distinguish a new attempt from a held input.
Trigger starts conditions. Harvest, Fishing, Build and Magic consume the relevant condition.

Freeze creates snow cover and clears it when clicked. The only current cover type is snow.
AI manages habitat population and creates or removes the visible fish. Individual hook attachment uses Hookable.
Freeze sets frozen and changes the affected terrain or object. Unit control restrictions also use Affectable.
Water advances these effects using its elapsed clock. Water terrain itself uses Immersible.
Damage reads this state on the attacker. The equipped weapon is referenced by Equippable, not stored here.
Push checks this marker on the entity initiating a push. A movable crate uses Displacable.
Start states with createSequence from Sequence. Dispose them with the Map helpers so their reference frames and particles are removed too.
Fate restores the saved appearance, vision and viewpoint when respawning. position is the return point, not the current Position.
Cactus creation still writes this legacy component, but the current Spike system reads getEntityStats(...).spike instead of SPIKABLE.damage. Attaching it does not enable contact damage.
Mounts Dimensions around the game's World, then renders the HUD, terminal and controls. The terminal owns the Three.js canvas; the other UI rows use character cells.
Positions the orthographic camera from useViewpoint. World x coordinates use the cell aspect ratio; world y is inverted for the renderer. Zoom follows the current cell height.
ExtendedStats mounts the renderer's FPS panel and an AVG panel on document.body. It removes the panel and animation callback when unmounted.
Wraps its children in DimensionsProvider and ScrollLock. React rendering and the container's CSS therefore use the same cell size and viewport bounds.
The div also registers with body-scroll-lock through enableBodyScroll.
Renders a counter against the maximum returned by getMaxCounter. Positive fractional values display at least one unit; scale and offsets come from the entity's stats.
Geometry comes from getBoxGeometry; materials are supplied as children. Reusing the geometry avoids allocating a new GPU buffer for every mounted box.
Renders the fixed fogOfWar sprite at fogHeight, without light or shadow shading. Entity decides when the overlay is needed from visibility and loot state; this component only draws it.
colorFactor darkens elevated stack layers. offsetZ keeps their order; LayerProps carries opacity, darkness and movement settings from Sprite.

The signature tracks light position, shadow range and map size, plus caster position, scale and geometry. A change sets shadowMap.needsUpdate. Mounting disables automatic updates; unmounting restores them.

World offsets are converted to renderer coordinates. The number of preceding glyph layers determines each segment's elevation. Segments with an animated origin use AnimatedSprite; the others use Sprite.

generation refreshes an entity after engine changes. inRadius, inside and outside provide the viewpoint and cover tests calculated by the surrounding renderer.

Room rendering uses worldRows, including native backdrops, equipment and facing. No combat simulation runs while reading a diagram.

Each family uses one GridTable: the name occupies the top-left header, variants occupy columns, and sprites, stats and properties occupy rows. Tables scroll horizontally while shared table headers keep the row and column labels visible. Empty values use empty cells.

Numeric-only inventory description rows are omitted when the comparison already shows their values. Negative action costs stay visible. Potion amounts and cooldowns come from consumptionConfigs. Drop distributions stay inside each family comparison. Every probability bundle uses the native Frame with a chance label and counted item references, including containers. Portraits in the same comparison share crop bounds; bosses and Golems use the real factory fragments and room diagrams instead of an enlarged single head.

Other cells use cellSnapshot from World Plants, so their icons come from the real cell factory, including layered flora and remains. Construction plots use the same plot sprite as performPlot, since they are not a cell-factory kind. Readable labels identify those cells; links point to the corresponding feature or plant family. Sprite mentions retain dialog gray, with the shared reference hover and underline behavior.

Draws a character-cell boundary over the game terminal. Feature scenes use a stationary viewpoint that yields to open dialogs at (6, 4) and hidden collision walls at x = -5 / 17, y = -3 / 11. The 23-column, 15-row frame occupies those same cells. Boundary walls cannot be harvested; normal scenes keep fog clear inside the frame, while Light retains interior fog and clears only its edges. Focus changes its color from silver to green. The action row starts half a cell below the frame line.

The index imports a reusable callout, the terminal palette and the CP437 character table through Markdown widgets. Colors come from orderedColors; names come from the game palette. Swatches use the actual colors without side decorations.
The font table uses codePage437, with hexadecimal row and column labels, compact cells and a surrounding frame. Control-symbol aliases match the game font.

portalMap creates the game's portal through createAreaWorld and selects its Warp tab. The map comes from the portal's original POPUP.lines; getWarpMap applies the same selection frame, offsets, lock color and player marker used by displayWarp.

WarpMap shows the full map with Dungeon selected from Menu. Its connection table reads levelConfig.warps. The enlarged portal combines the portal and vortex sprites as the game does.

Catalog families render comparison tables through CatalogEntry. Class columns use getLevelStats for levels 1-11 and the original class sprites and backdrops. Animals includes the chick unit, worm bait, and catch item representations from the fishing data. Fish item art does not imply a distinct ambient creature sprite.
The damage calculator lives in Damage. The command builder uses completeCommand; Run sends the command to the real engine preview.

Plant comparisons use createCell in a small area world. This includes flora created directly in the cell factory rather than through unitDefinitions: trees, palms, oak, bushes and grass, including fruit-bearing variants. The shared worldRows compositor orders the actual body, backdrop and inventory layers with their facing and quantity variants; work and yields come from their actual harvest resource. Combat plants remain in the unit catalog.

itemVariants starts with crafting, brewing, trading, building and unit equipment/drop definitions. Configured forge bases and their reachable upgrade results are included through getForgeOptions. Variants need a real inventory sprite and meaningful balancing stats, or a functional consumable, map or compass definition. Unsupported artwork is not treated as an available tier.

unitComparisonStats creates only equipment records in a minimal ECS and calls getEntityDisplayStats, so displayed attributes include equipped bonuses and the same haste/vision offsets as the game. Attack rows use the NPC caster's balancing overrides, including concealed weapons. Stat pickup entries require a production recipe, trade or unit reference; command-only aliases remain available in the command documentation.

completeCommand(input) returns full command-line suggestions. It reads command names and aliases from commandSignatures, item names from commandItems, and argument values from the engine's item, stat, NPC, and cell definitions.

The preview server rebuilds and reloads the browser after Markdown, React, CSS, font or build-script changes. The current URL stays open. Page content comes from Markdown in docs/ and src/. Links resolve to generated HTML.

App.tsx renders Markdown tokens in React and handles browser history. Routes follow menu groups under game-design/ and development/; Welcome remains index.html. Each route has a generated HTML shell, so direct links work on static hosting. Old flat URLs remain aliases. GamePreview.tsx manages isolated frames; preview.tsx mounts the game. Widgets.tsx imports game tables and calculators. visuals.tsx uses the shared Row and composed glyph helper for selectable text.

The workflow builds the game and docs, then publishes build/ to gh-pages. The runner is pinned to Ubuntu 24.04 for Playwright support.
The dev server builds into .docs-dev/, separately from the static build, so running both does not replace files underneath the watcher.

Write a module's purpose and important contracts in its adjacent Markdown file before running docs:types. The generator refreshes declarations below <!-- source-types --> and preserves authored examples above it. A missing source note stops generation before files are changed.

The URL carries ?test#scene/option. Feature scenes use a stationary viewpoint that yields to dialogs. Their 23-by-15 frame is centered on the actual Terminal box, including its native pixel overscan. Touch starts also activate focus, so both native and emulated gestures highlight the boundary. Audio is muted. Navigation keys are captured inside the frame so they cannot scroll the documentation. Position and health messages support the command and damage tools.

createPreviewWorld composes a small level with createAreaWorld, createCell, and populateInventory. Each scene has a Rogue, its required equipment and resources, and a target or workstation. The static Interface diagram imports the Island spawn area; it does not run an interactive scene. Feature scenes have a stationary viewpoint that yields to dialogs and collision walls aligned with the 23-by-15 visible frame. Ordinary scenes reveal exactly that rectangle. Light keeps the mechanic's interior fog, while every boundary remains visible. The Touch scene sends emulated mouse gestures through the game's normal touch handlers.

inspection.method: Entire pages were scrolled, then full-page and local code/table overflow screenshots were inspected as 348 image bands in 87 contact sheets. Sheets000–076 were inspected by tables_links; catalog_previews inspected077–086 and appended lower028 content.
inspection.limitations: Desktop route audit used Chromium with --disable-gpu. Subsequent native-font regression probes used normal GPU at desktop and phone sizes; targeted catalog captures and root aggregate checks cover final shared changes. Screenshots are evidence at capture time, not a claim that all source documentation was re-researched exhaustively.
